chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Rahim, who said:

I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him), 'The Ziyarah of the grave of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) in Baghdad involves difficulty for us. What is the reward for one who visits him?' He said to him, 'The same as the reward for one who goes to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).'

He said, 'And a man entered, said Salam to him, and sat down. He mentioned Baghdad and the inferiority of its people, and what was expected to befall them from the earth swallowing them, the clamor, and the lightning bolts, and enumerated from those things some items.'
He said, 'So I stood up to leave, and I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying, 'As for Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), none (of this will affect him).'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam Musa al-Kadhim in Baghdad?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (a.s.) equates the spiritual reward of visiting Imam al-Kadhim’s grave in Baghdad to that of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.), validating the significance of the Kadhimiyya shrine despite the geographical hardships. The narration highlights the eschatological trials awaiting the people of Baghdad, such as the *khasf* (sinking) and *sa'yha* (cry), yet concludes with the phrase 'Amma Abul Hasan fa-la' (As for Abu al-Hasan, [he is safe/there is no such thing for him]), affirming the Imam’s distinct status and protection from these specific calamities.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 10. Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan Al-Saffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from ‘Ali ibn Ḥakam, from Raḥīm, who said:

I said to Imam Riďā (s.a.a.w.), “We face some difficulties when we go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Abil Ḥasan (Imam Kāżim (a.s.)) in Baghdad. What are the rewards for those who go to his Ziyārah?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “Its rewards are the same as the rewards for going to (the Ziyārah of) the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.).”

(After Imam (a.s.) said this) a man entered, said Salām to the Imam (a.s.), and sat down. He started talking about Baghdad and the inferiority of its people and about the afflictions, the collapsing of the earth, the clamour, and the bolts of lightning which are expected to befall Baghdad.
Then I got up to leave and I heard Abal Ḥasan (Imam Riďā (a.s.)) say, “As for Abul Ḥasan (Imam Kāżim (a.s.)), none (of this will affect him).”
